standard_prerequisites: The associated points of the fibres of a finite type quasicoherent module, and their behaviour under etale base change
Etale charts of a morphism and continuity of the induced map on underlying topological spaces, so that specializations can be compared

The notion of a decent algebraic space and of a decent morphism, the representation of a point of a decent space by a quasi-compact monomorphism, and the lifting of specializations along a decent morphism
The corresponding criterion in the case of schemes
core_obligations: Assume the second condition and choose etale charts of the target and of the fibre product, together with a point of the chart mapping to the given point

Identify the associated points of the fibre of the pulled back module with the fibre of the associated points of the original module, and note that specializations in the fibre of the chart map to specializations in the fibre of the original morphism, so that the hypothesis is inherited by the chart
Apply the scheme case of the criterion to the chart and conclude flatness at the chosen point, which gives the implication from the second condition to the first

For the converse assume the spaces decent, represent the image point by a quasi-compact monomorphism and identify the fibre with the fibre product over the residue field, then use that the fibre stays decent and that specializations lift along the chart to transfer the criterion from the scheme case back
proof_roadmap: Push the hypothesis to an etale chart and compare associated points and specializations
Apply the scheme case to get flatness at the point
In the decent case lift specializations along the chart and use the scheme case for the converse
difficulty_reason: The counted conclusion is the flatness criterion at the associated points of the fibre at source lines 834-850, label theorem-check-flatness-at-associated-points, whose proof occupies source lines 852-887. The proof reduces the statement to the scheme case through etale charts, and the reduction is where the content lies: the associated points of the fibre of the pulled back module must be identified with the fibre of the associated points of the original module, and one must check that the hypothesis is inherited, which uses continuity of the map on underlying spaces to compare specializations. The converse direction is not automatic and needs decentness: the image point is represented by a quasi-compact monomorphism, the fibre is identified as the fibre product over the residue field, the fibre of a decent morphism is decent, and specializations lift along the chart, which is what allows the scheme case to be applied backwards. The counted statement records neither the chart reduction nor the decentness input.
